facts.function: Large fan-shaped upper part of the hip bone; forms upper acetabulum; iliac crest and spines are key palpable landmarks
facts.attachments: Iliacus (fossa), gluteal muscles (outer surface), abdominal wall muscles and inguinal ligament (crest/ASIS)

facts.function: Smooth concave internal surface of the ala forming the posterolateral wall of the greater pelvis
facts.attachments: Origin of iliacus; bounded below by the arcuate line, behind by the auricular surface

facts.function: Palpable superior border of the ilium from ASIS to PSIS; highest point at L4 (supracristal plane, lumbar puncture landmark)
facts.attachments: Abdominal wall muscles, latissimus dorsi, quadratus lumborum, fascia lata; bone marrow biopsy site

facts.function: Palpable anterior end of the iliac crest; surface landmark for the inguinal ligament and limb-length measurement
facts.attachments: Sartorius, tensor fasciae latae, lateral end of inguinal ligament; avulsion by sartorius in sprinters

facts.function: Projection on the anterior ilium just above the acetabulum
facts.attachments: Straight head of rectus femoris and the iliofemoral ligament; rectus femoris avulsion site (kicking)

facts.function: Posteroinferior part of the hip bone; forms posterior acetabulum and bears weight when sitting
facts.attachments: Hamstrings, adductor magnus (hamstring part), sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, gemelli

facts.function: Separates greater from lesser sciatic notch; landmark for pudendal nerve block (nerve passes behind it)
facts.attachments: Sacrospinous ligament, superior gemellus, coccygeus, levator ani (tendinous arch)

facts.function: Weight-bearing "sit bone"; common origin of the hamstrings (hamstring avulsion site)
facts.attachments: Semitendinosus, semimembranosus, long head biceps femoris, hamstring part of adductor magnus, quadratus femoris, sacrotuberous ligament

facts.function: Anteromedial part of the hip bone; forms anterior acetabulum and anterior pelvic ring with the opposite pubis
facts.attachments: Adductors, gracilis, pectineus, rectus abdominis, inguinal ligament

facts.function: Upper border of the obturator foramen; carries the pectineal line; obturator canal lies beneath it
facts.attachments: Pectineus (pectineal line), lacunar and pectineal ligaments; joins the body to the acetabulum

facts.function: Joins the ischial ramus (ischiopubic ramus) below the obturator foramen; part of the pubic arch
facts.attachments: Adductor brevis, gracilis, adductor magnus (adductor part), obturator externus

facts.function: Palpable anterior projection; medial attachment of the inguinal ligament; superficial inguinal ring lies just above
facts.attachments: Inguinal ligament; adductor longus tendon arises just below

facts.function: Secondary cartilaginous joint (fibrocartilaginous interpubic disc) uniting the pubic bodies; slight movement, widens in pregnancy
facts.attachments: Superior and inferior (arcuate) pubic ligaments reinforce it

facts.function: Notches on the posterior border of the hip bone converted into foramina by the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments
Above the ischial spine; becomes the greater sciatic foramen (piriformis, gluteal vessels/nerves, sciatic, pudendal)
facts.attachments: Bounded by the sacrospinous ligament below and sacrotuberous ligament behind

facts.function: Below the ischial spine; becomes the lesser sciatic foramen (obturator internus tendon, pudendal nerve/internal pudendal vessels, nerve to OI)
facts.attachments: Between sacrospinous (above) and sacrotuberous (below) ligaments; OI tendon turns over its cartilage-covered surface

facts.function: Opening between pubis and ischium closed by the obturator membrane except the obturator canal (obturator nerve and vessels)
facts.attachments: Obturator internus (inner) and obturator externus (outer) arise from membrane and margins

facts.function: Deep cup-shaped socket for the femoral head; deeper than the glenoid so the hip is more stable than the shoulder
facts.attachments: Formed by ilium, ischium, pubis (Y-shaped cartilage); lunate surface, acetabular fossa and notch; labrum on rim

facts.function: Head articulates with the acetabulum; neck angles it ~125° to the shaft; neck fractures risk avascular necrosis of the head
facts.supply: Mainly medial circumflex femoral (retinacular arteries); minor: lateral circumflex, artery of ligament of head

facts.function: Smooth ~2/3 sphere articulating with the acetabulum; fovea for the ligament of the head
facts.supply: Retinacular branches of medial circumflex femoral; small contribution from artery of ligament of head (obturator)

facts.function: Joins head to shaft at ~125°; intracapsular fractures (elderly falls) tear retinacular arteries causing AVN
facts.attachments: Hip joint capsule attaches to intertrochanteric line anteriorly; retinacula carry vessels along it

facts.function: Muscle-attachment prominences at the neck-shaft junction, joined by the intertrochanteric line (front) and crest (back)
Palpable lateral prominence; lever for the hip abductors and lateral rotators; trochanteric bursitis site
facts.attachments: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus, piriformis, obturator internus, gemelli; obturator externus into trochanteric fossa

facts.function: Posteromedial projection below the neck; insertion of the principal hip flexor
facts.attachments: Iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus)

facts.function: Fibrocartilage ring on the acetabular rim deepening the socket and gripping the femoral head; tears cause hip pain/clicking (impingement)
facts.attachments: Acetabular rim; bridged across the acetabular notch by the transverse acetabular ligament

facts.function: Weak intracapsular band; little stabilizing role; conduit for the artery of the ligament of the head
facts.attachments: Acetabular notch/transverse acetabular ligament → fovea of the femoral head
facts.supply: Carries the acetabular branch of the obturator artery to the head

facts.function: Gluteal muscles: maximus extends hip; medius/minimus abduct and stabilize the pelvis in stance
facts.innervation: Maximus: inferior gluteal (L5–S2); medius/minimus: superior gluteal (L4–S1)

facts.function: Main hip extensor (rising, stairs, running) and lateral rotator; little use in level walking
facts.attachments: Ilium behind posterior gluteal line, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament → IT tract and gluteal tuberosity

facts.function: Abducts and medially rotates thigh; keeps pelvis level in single-leg stance (Trendelenburg sign if weak)
facts.attachments: Outer ilium between anterior and posterior gluteal lines → lateral greater trochanter

facts.function: Abducts and medially rotates thigh; stabilizes pelvis with gluteus medius
facts.attachments: Outer ilium between anterior and inferior gluteal lines → anterior greater trochanter

facts.function: TFL tenses the IT tract; together they abduct, medially rotate and flex the hip and stabilize the extended knee
Abducts and medially rotates thigh; assists hip flexion; tenses IT tract to steady the knee
facts.attachments: ASIS and anterior iliac crest → iliotibial tract
facts.supply: Superior gluteal and lateral circumflex femoral arteries

facts.function: Thickened lateral fascia lata; stabilizes hip and extended knee; friction over lateral epicondyle causes IT band syndrome
facts.attachments: Iliac tubercle, TFL and gluteus maximus → anterolateral (Gerdy) tubercle of the lateral tibial condyle

facts.function: Laterally rotates extended thigh, abducts flexed thigh; key landmark of the gluteal region (piriformis syndrome compresses sciatic)
facts.attachments: Anterior sacrum (S2–S4) → through greater sciatic foramen → superior border of greater trochanter

facts.function: Laterally rotates extended thigh, abducts flexed thigh; stabilizes femoral head in acetabulum
facts.attachments: Pelvic surface of obturator membrane and margins → turns through lesser sciatic foramen → medial greater trochanter

facts.function: Small muscles flanking the obturator internus tendon; laterally rotate thigh, steady femoral head
Laterally rotates extended thigh; reinforces obturator internus tendon
facts.attachments: Ischial spine → obturator internus tendon → medial greater trochanter

facts.function: Laterally rotates extended thigh; reinforces obturator internus tendon
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity (upper part) → obturator internus tendon → medial greater trochanter

facts.function: Strong lateral rotator of the thigh
facts.attachments: Lateral ischial tuberosity → quadrate tubercle on intertrochanteric crest

facts.function: Laterally rotates thigh; steadies femoral head; medial-compartment muscle that does not adduct
facts.attachments: External surface of obturator membrane and margins → trochanteric fossa of femur
facts.supply: Obturator and medial circumflex femoral arteries

facts.function: Exit from pelvis to gluteal region: piriformis; above it superior gluteal vessels/nerve; below it sciatic, inferior gluteal, pudendal, posterior femoral cutaneous
facts.attachments: Greater sciatic notch closed by sacrospinous (below) and sacrotuberous (behind) ligaments

facts.function: Contains, lateral to medial, femoral nerve, artery, vein, lymphatics (NAVeL); femoral pulse and catheter access site
facts.attachments: Inguinal ligament (base), sartorius medial border (lateral), adductor longus medial border (medial); floor iliopsoas, pectineus, adductor longus

facts.function: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates thigh; flexes knee ("tailor's position"); roof of adductor canal
facts.attachments: ASIS → superomedial tibia (pes anserinus)

facts.function: Extends knee and flexes hip (crosses both joints); only quadriceps head acting at the hip
facts.attachments: AIIS (straight head) and above acetabulum (reflected head) → quadriceps tendon, patella, patellar ligament → tibial tuberosity

facts.function: The three vasti extend the knee via the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament
Extends knee; largest quadriceps head; common IM injection site in infants
facts.attachments: Greater trochanter and lateral lip of linea aspera → quadriceps tendon → tibial tuberosity

facts.function: Extends knee; oblique lower fibers pull patella medially, resisting lateral patellar dislocation
facts.attachments: Intertrochanteric line and medial lip of linea aspera → quadriceps tendon, medial patella → tibial tuberosity

facts.function: Extends knee; lies deep to rectus femoris on the femoral shaft
facts.attachments: Anterior and lateral femoral shaft → quadriceps tendon → tibial tuberosity

facts.function: Medial compartment adductors of the thigh; adductor longus and brevis also assist hip flexion
facts.innervation: Obturator nerve (L2–L4); hamstring part of magnus by tibial division of sciatic

facts.function: Adducts thigh, assists flexion; anterior and posterior obturator divisions lie on either side of it
facts.attachments: Body and inferior ramus of pubis → pectineal line and upper linea aspera

facts.function: Adducts thigh, assists flexion; medial border of femoral triangle; groin strain muscle
facts.attachments: Body of pubis below pubic crest → middle third of linea aspera

facts.function: Largest adductor: adductor part adducts thigh; hamstring part extends hip
facts.innervation: Adductor part: obturator nerve; hamstring part: tibial division of sciatic (L4)
facts.attachments: Ischiopubic ramus and ischial tuberosity → gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera, adductor tubercle

facts.function: Adductor magnus is a hybrid muscle: an adductor part and a hamstring part with different actions and nerves
facts.innervation: Dual: obturator nerve (adductor part) and tibial division of sciatic (hamstring part)

facts.function: Adducts the thigh
facts.attachments: Ischiopubic ramus → gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera, medial supracondylar line

facts.function: Extends the thigh at the hip (acts like a hamstring but not on the knee)
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity → adductor tubercle of femur; its tendon bounds the adductor hiatus

facts.function: Passageway from femoral triangle apex to adductor hiatus for femoral artery, femoral vein, saphenous nerve, nerve to vastus medialis
facts.attachments: Roof sartorius (vastoadductor membrane); anterolateral vastus medialis; posteromedial adductor longus and magnus

facts.function: Adducts thigh; flexes and medially rotates the leg at the knee; expendable graft muscle
facts.attachments: Body and inferior ramus of pubis → superomedial tibia (pes anserinus)

facts.function: Adducts and flexes thigh; transitional muscle in floor of femoral triangle
facts.attachments: Pectineal line of superior pubic ramus → pectineal line of femur below lesser trochanter
facts.supply: Medial circumflex femoral and obturator arteries

facts.function: Extends hip, flexes knee, medially rotates flexed leg
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity → superomedial tibia (pes anserinus); long cord-like tendon

facts.function: Extends hip, flexes knee, medially rotates flexed leg
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity → posterior medial tibial condyle; expansions form oblique popliteal ligament

facts.function: Extends hip, flexes knee, laterally rotates flexed leg
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity (with semitendinosus) → head of fibula

facts.function: Lateral hamstring: flexes knee and laterally rotates flexed leg; long head also extends hip
facts.innervation: Long head tibial division; short head common fibular division of sciatic

facts.function: Extends hip, flexes knee, laterally rotates flexed leg
facts.attachments: Ischial tuberosity → head of fibula

facts.function: Flexes knee and laterally rotates flexed leg; only hamstring muscle not crossing the hip
facts.innervation: Common fibular division of sciatic nerve (L5–S2) - the exception
facts.attachments: Lateral lip of linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line → head of fibula

facts.function: Motor to gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and TFL; injury → Trendelenburg sign (pelvis drops on unsupported side)
facts.innervation: L4–S1 (posterior divisions of sacral plexus); motor only
facts.attachments: Exits greater sciatic foramen above piriformis with superior gluteal vessels; runs between gluteus medius and minimus

facts.function: Motor to gluteus maximus; injury → weak hip extension (difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair)
facts.attachments: Exits greater sciatic foramen below piriformis with inferior gluteal vessels → deep surface of gluteus maximus

facts.function: Motor to piriformis
facts.attachments: Arises within the pelvis and enters the anterior (pelvic) surface of piriformis

facts.function: Motor to obturator internus and superior gemellus
facts.attachments: Below piriformis → crosses ischial spine with pudendal nerve → lesser sciatic foramen → pelvic surface of obturator internus

facts.function: Motor to quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus; also an articular branch to the hip
facts.attachments: Below piriformis, deep to sciatic nerve and to gemelli/obturator internus tendon → quadratus femoris

facts.function: Motor to anterior thigh (quadriceps, sartorius, iliacus, pectineus); sensory anteromedial thigh and, via saphenous, medial leg; injury → weak knee extension
facts.innervation: L2–L4 (posterior divisions of lumbar plexus); motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Between psoas and iliacus → under inguinal ligament lateral to femoral artery, outside femoral sheath → branches in femoral triangle

facts.function: Motor to medial thigh adductors (and obturator externus, gracilis); sensory medial thigh; injury → weak adduction, leg swings outward
facts.innervation: L2–L4 (anterior divisions of lumbar plexus); motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Medial border of psoas → lateral pelvic wall → obturator canal → anterior and posterior divisions around adductor brevis

facts.function: Largest nerve: motor to hamstrings, hamstring part of adductor magnus and all leg/foot muscles; sensory most of leg and foot
facts.innervation: L4–S3 (sacral plexus); tibial and common fibular divisions in one sheath; motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Greater sciatic foramen below piriformis → between greater trochanter and ischial tuberosity → deep to biceps femoris → splits at popliteal apex

facts.function: Supplies hamstrings (except short head of biceps) and hamstring part of adductor magnus; continues as tibial nerve to posterior leg and sole
facts.innervation: L4–S3 (anterior divisions of sacral plexus); motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Medial part of the sciatic nerve; becomes the tibial nerve at the popliteal apex, running down the middle of the fossa

facts.function: Supplies short head of biceps femoris; continues as common fibular nerve to anterior and lateral leg; injury at fibular neck → foot drop
facts.innervation: L4–S2 (posterior divisions of sacral plexus); motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Lateral part of the sciatic nerve; follows medial border of biceps femoris, winds around the fibular neck

facts.function: Rounded distal femoral expansions articulating with the tibial condyles and menisci; patellar surface in front, intercondylar fossa behind
Larger medial articular condyle; bears much of the load; PCL attaches to its lateral (notch) surface
facts.attachments: Medial epicondyle and adductor tubercle above; tibial collateral ligament, medial gastrocnemius head

facts.function: Lateral articular condyle; ACL attaches to its medial (notch) surface; anterior part buttresses the patella laterally
facts.attachments: Lateral epicondyle; fibular collateral ligament, lateral gastrocnemius head, popliteus

facts.function: Anterior grooved articular surface for the patella; prominent lateral lip resists lateral patellar dislocation
facts.attachments: Patellofemoral joint; continuous with the condylar articular surfaces below

facts.function: Deep notch between the femoral condyles housing the cruciate ligaments
facts.attachments: ACL on medial surface of lateral condyle; PCL on lateral surface of medial condyle

facts.function: Medial weight-bearing bone of the leg; transmits body weight from femur to talus
facts.attachments: Condyles articulate with femur (knee); tuberosity receives patellar ligament; pes anserinus medially; medial malleolus at ankle

facts.function: Flat superior articular surfaces of the tibial condyles that bear load across the knee; menisci improve congruity with femoral condyles
facts.attachments: Menisci and cruciates attach to intercondylar areas between the plateaus; plateau fractures follow valgus impact

facts.function: Expanded proximal ends of the tibia bearing body weight through the knee
Larger medial condyle carrying the medial plateau
facts.attachments: Semimembranosus (posteromedial groove); tibial collateral ligament below; medial meniscus via coronary ligament

facts.function: Lateral condyle carrying the lateral plateau; articulates with the fibular head below (proximal tibiofibular joint)
facts.attachments: Iliotibial tract on Gerdy tubercle (anterolateral); tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus origins

facts.function: Raised central ridge (medial and lateral intercondylar tubercles) between the plateaus; can avulse with ACL injury
facts.attachments: ACL and meniscal horns attach to the anterior intercondylar area; PCL to the posterior area

facts.function: Anterior prominence below the condyles transmitting quadriceps force; Osgood-Schlatter disease in adolescents
facts.attachments: Patellar ligament

facts.function: Largest sesamoid bone, in quadriceps tendon; increases the extensor lever arm and protects the knee
facts.attachments: Quadriceps tendon (base) → patellar ligament (apex); articulates with patellar surface of femur

facts.function: Slender lateral leg bone; not weight-bearing and not part of the knee joint; muscle attachment and lateral ankle stability
facts.attachments: Head: biceps femoris, fibular collateral ligament; common fibular nerve winds around its neck; lateral malleolus at ankle

facts.function: Transmits pull of the quadriceps to the patella; rupture → loss of active knee extension
facts.attachments: Rectus femoris and three vasti → base of patella; continues as patellar ligament

facts.function: Continuation of the quadriceps tendon below the patella; tapped for the patellar (knee-jerk) reflex L3–L4
facts.attachments: Apex of patella → tibial tuberosity

facts.function: Fibrocartilage wedges deepening the tibial plateaus: improve congruity, absorb shock, spread load; medial meniscus tears more often
facts.supply: Genicular arteries to the peripheral (red) zone only; inner zone avascular, heals poorly

facts.function: C-shaped, less mobile; fused to the tibial collateral ligament so often torn with it (unhappy triad)
facts.attachments: Anterior and posterior horns to intercondylar areas; periphery to capsule and tibial collateral ligament

facts.function: Nearly circular, more mobile; separated from the fibular collateral ligament by the popliteus tendon
facts.attachments: Horns to intercondylar area close together; meniscofemoral ligaments to medial femoral condyle

facts.function: Prevents anterior displacement of the tibia on the femur and hyperextension; torn in pivoting/valgus injuries; anterior drawer and Lachman tests
facts.attachments: Anterior intercondylar area of tibia → posteromedial surface of lateral femoral condyle

facts.function: Prevents posterior displacement of the tibia (dashboard injury); stronger than ACL; posterior drawer test
facts.attachments: Posterior intercondylar area of tibia → anterolateral surface of medial femoral condyle

facts.function: Collateral ligaments stabilize the knee side-to-side and are taut in extension
Resists valgus (lateral blow) stress; injured with ACL and medial meniscus in the unhappy triad
facts.attachments: Medial femoral epicondyle → medial tibial condyle and shaft; fused to medial meniscus

facts.function: Resists varus (medial blow) stress; cord-like and separate from the capsule and lateral meniscus
facts.attachments: Lateral femoral epicondyle → head of fibula

facts.function: Base of the femoral triangle; femoral nerve, artery, vein pass beneath; landmark for hernias (inguinal above, femoral below)
facts.attachments: ASIS → pubic tubercle; inrolled lower edge of external oblique aponeurosis

facts.function: Gap through which the femoral vessels pass from the adductor canal into the popliteal fossa, becoming popliteal artery and vein
facts.attachments: Between adductor (aponeurotic) and hamstring (tendinous) insertions of adductor magnus, above the adductor tubercle

facts.function: Diamond behind knee containing (superficial to deep) tibial and common fibular nerves, popliteal vein, popliteal artery; popliteal pulse, Baker cyst
facts.attachments: Biceps femoris (superolateral), semimembranosus/semitendinosus (superomedial), gastrocnemius heads (inferior); floor femur, capsule, popliteus

facts.function: Supplies pelvis and lower limb
facts.attachments: Aortic bifurcation at L4 → divides in front of sacroiliac joint into internal and external iliac arteries

facts.function: Terminal branches of the common iliac: internal supplies pelvis/gluteal region/medial thigh; external supplies the lower limb
Supplies pelvic organs, perineum, gluteal region and medial thigh
facts.attachments: Common iliac at sacroiliac joint → posterior division (superior gluteal) and anterior division (inferior gluteal, obturator, internal pudendal, visceral)

facts.function: Main arterial supply to the lower limb
facts.attachments: Common iliac → along pelvic brim on psoas → becomes femoral artery under the inguinal ligament; gives inferior epigastric, deep circumflex iliac

facts.function: Internal iliac branches supplying the gluteal region through the greater sciatic foramen
Supplies gluteus medius, minimus, TFL and maximus; contributes to trochanteric anastomosis
facts.attachments: Posterior division of internal iliac → greater sciatic foramen above piriformis with superior gluteal nerve

facts.function: Supplies gluteus maximus and posterior thigh; joins the cruciate anastomosis
facts.attachments: Anterior division of internal iliac → greater sciatic foramen below piriformis

facts.function: Supplies medial thigh (adductors) and gives the artery of the ligament of the head of the femur
facts.attachments: Anterior division of internal iliac → lateral pelvic wall → obturator canal → anterior and posterior branches

facts.function: Main artery of the thigh; femoral pulse below the mid-inguinal point; arterial catheterization site
facts.attachments: External iliac under inguinal ligament → femoral triangle → adductor canal → adductor hiatus → popliteal artery

facts.function: Common femoral above the profunda origin; "superficial femoral" (clinical term) below it, continuing to the adductor hiatus
facts.attachments: Common femoral ~4 cm below inguinal ligament gives deep femoral; superficial femoral runs through the adductor canal

facts.function: Main supply of the thigh muscles and femoral head (via circumflex femoral arteries)
facts.attachments: Lateral/posterior side of femoral artery → behind adductor longus → circumflex femorals and perforating arteries

facts.function: Main supply of the thigh, especially posterior and medial compartments, and of the femoral head and neck via its circumflex branches
facts.attachments: Femoral artery ~4 cm below inguinal ligament → deep to adductor longus → medial and lateral circumflex femoral, 3–4 perforating arteries

facts.function: Supply the hamstrings, adductor magnus and vastus lateralis; first perforating joins the cruciate anastomosis
facts.attachments: Deep femoral artery → pierce adductor magnus close to the linea aspera → posterior compartment

facts.function: Circumflex femoral arteries encircle the proximal femur, forming trochanteric and cruciate anastomoses
Principal supply to femoral head and neck via retinacular arteries; damaged in neck fractures → AVN
facts.attachments: Deep femoral (sometimes femoral) → between pectineus and iliopsoas → posteriorly to trochanteric fossa

facts.function: Supplies anterior thigh muscles and greater trochanter; minor femoral head supply; descending branch runs on vastus lateralis
facts.attachments: Deep femoral → laterally deep to sartorius and rectus femoris → ascending, transverse, descending branches

facts.function: Main blood supply of the femoral head; torn in displaced intracapsular neck fractures → avascular necrosis
facts.attachments: Medial circumflex femoral (trochanteric fossa) → along posterosuperior femoral neck under the retinacula → head-neck junction

facts.function: Minor supply to the femoral head near the fovea; important in children, insufficient alone in adults
facts.attachments: Acetabular branch of obturator artery → acetabular notch → along ligament of head → fovea

facts.function: Supplies knee (genicular arteries) and calf muscles (sural); popliteal pulse felt deep in fossa with knee flexed; injured in knee dislocation
facts.attachments: Femoral artery at adductor hiatus → deepest structure in popliteal fossa → divides at lower popliteus into anterior and posterior tibial

facts.function: Longest superficial vein; varicose veins; harvested for coronary bypass grafts
facts.attachments: Medial dorsal venous arch → anterior to medial malleolus → medial leg/thigh → saphenous opening → femoral vein below inguinal ligament

facts.function: Main deep vein of the thigh; common DVT site (embolism risk); central line access medial to femoral pulse
facts.attachments: Popliteal vein at adductor hiatus → adductor canal → femoral triangle medial to artery → external iliac vein under inguinal ligament

facts.function: Superficial vein draining the lateral foot and posterior leg
facts.attachments: Lateral dorsal venous arch → behind lateral malleolus → up the midline calf with sural nerve → popliteal vein in popliteal fossa

facts.function: Deep vein of the knee region; DVT here causes leg swelling and risks pulmonary embolism
facts.attachments: Union of anterior and posterior tibial veins (plus small saphenous) → superficial to popliteal artery → femoral vein at adductor hiatus

facts.function: Deep veins returning blood from the lower limb (external) and pelvis/gluteal region (internal)
Drains the lower limb
facts.attachments: Femoral vein at inguinal ligament → along pelvic brim medial to the artery → joins internal iliac vein

facts.function: Drains pelvic organs, perineum and gluteal region
facts.attachments: Gluteal, obturator, pudendal and visceral tributaries → joins external iliac vein in front of sacroiliac joint

facts.function: Returns blood from the pelvis and lower limb to the IVC; left one compressed by right common iliac artery (May-Thurner)
facts.attachments: External + internal iliac veins at sacroiliac joint → unite at L5 (right side) to form the inferior vena cava
